clue.text: English medic's back on the job — that'll make delivery easier

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: back tells us to read the English-plus-medic pair from right to left

parts.note: a doc is a doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: An English doctor returns to work, and something is said to ease a delivery, perhaps of a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the English medic, and 'on' puts it after the job. The delivery sounds like a baby's but is the postman's.
explanation.definitionFit: A postal code on an envelope helps the mail service route and deliver letters.

clue.text: An old Jew's harp in need of repair, I understand

indicators.note: in need of repair suggests something broken that has to be put back together in a new form

parts.note: to see is to understand

explanation.surface: An instrument called a Jew's harp is broken, someone gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in need of repair' rearranges HARP + I into PHARI. The surface invites a Jew's harp; the split is after 'Jew', with 's as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pharisees were a strict sect of ancient Judaism.

clue.text: The trick is to serve up exceedingly good pastries

indicators.note: in a down clue serve up turns the whole run upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: mega is slang for excellent
tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: The secret is to serve wonderful pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve up' reverses MEGA + TARTS together.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning plan or ruse.

clue.text: Church leader soon to become a priest

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word church

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A churchman will shortly be ordained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church leader' looks like a bishop, but it is just the letter C.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral.

clue.text: Ship wrecked below embankment only slightly wet

indicators.note: below in a down clue places the wrecked ship under the embankment

parts.note: a dam is an embankment holding back water

indicators.note: wrecked means the letters of ship are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A ship lies wrecked beneath a sea wall, only a little damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' turns SHIP into PISH, placed 'below' DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Dampish means somewhat moist, a little damp.

clue.text: Salute move to take in Greek island

indicators.note: to take in means the first piece swallows the second, holding it inside

parts.note: to act is to move or take action
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: Someone makes a gesture of greeting while planning a trip to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' sets the island inside the move. 'Salute' is a greeting here, not a military gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them, a forward kind of greeting.

clue.text: Dry places ruined this old timer

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of the phrase are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Dry places have spoilt an old-timer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges DRY PLACES. An 'old timer' is a veteran, but here a timing device.
explanation.definitionFit: A clepsydra is an ancient water clock that measured time by flowing water.

clue.text: The Way of the World?

parts.note: the path a planet such as ours takes around the sun, read literally

explanation.surface: The title of a Restoration comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Way of the World is Congreve's play, but here 'way' is a path through space.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earth's path around the sun is its circuit through space.

clue.text: Not the practice, presumably, of the Circle Line

parts.note: a circle is the letter O by its shape
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Something about the London Underground's Circle Line in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presumably, of' links. The Circle Line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: Theory and practice are opposites: one is abstract principle, the other application.

clue.text: Peter out? Cricket side produces a bottle of wine

parts.note: to flag is to tire or peter out
on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A man called Peter is out, so the cricket team brings wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' reads as a name; it is the verb to peter out. In cricket the on (leg) side is one half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagon is a large vessel or bottle for wine.

clue.text: Part of stage used for Pinafore

definitions.meaning: the forestage in front of the curtain in a theatre
a protective garment worn over clothes

explanation.surface: Something from the stage is borrowed for a production of the operetta HMS Pinafore.
explanation.walkthrough: The italic Pinafore suggests the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, but it is simply the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: The stage sense is the area in front of the proscenium; the garment sense is a covering tied over clothes.

clue.text: Polo-stick's most effective in plastic

parts.note: a polo stick is a mallet, so when it does its job best it is, punningly, able as a mallet

explanation.surface: A polo player's stick works best when made of plastic.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun splits the answer as 'mallet-able': a polo stick at its best. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a material that can be shaped or moulded easily.

clue.text: Contemplating short international final

parts.note: Int is the shortened form of international
a final is an ending

explanation.surface: Someone is considering a brief international match before a final.
explanation.definitionFit: Intending to do something means planning or having it in mind.

clue.text: Troublesome stray goat

indicators.note: troublesome signals that the letters of the next word are unruly and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A goat that has wandered off is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublesome' rearranges STRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a satyr is a woodland creature, half man and half goat.

clue.text: Tongue of land set in the silver sea

definitions.text: Tongue of land set in the silver sea

parts.words: Tongue of land set in the silver sea
parts.note: the language of the country Shakespeare's John of Gaunt describes as a precious stone set in the silver sea

explanation.surface: A promontory juts out into a shining sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue of land' looks like a spit or headland, but tongue means language, and the land is England from Richard II's 'This precious stone set in the silver sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: The national language of England is the one named after the country.

clue.text: Make oneself liable for debts without interest

parts.note: to incur a debt is to bring it upon oneself
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Taking on debts that carry no interest charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' suggests a financial charge, but here it means curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Incurious means lacking curiosity, uninterested.

clue.text: Narrow margin of victory, with party squeezing in? Get knotted!

indicators.note: squeezing in means the party is pushed inside the victory margin

parts.note: a race won by a nose is won by the narrowest margin
a do is a party

explanation.surface: After a close win a party crashes in, and someone is told rudely to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezing in' puts the party inside the winning margin. 'Get knotted!' reads as a rude dismissal, but 'knotted' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodose is a botanical word for having knots or knobbly swellings.

clue.text: Good job one remains upright in a fiddle!

definitions.text: one remains upright in a fiddle!

parts.note: sound means good or reliable
a post is a job

explanation.surface: Someone has a good job keeping honest in a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests fraud, but it is a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wooden peg inside a violin stands between belly and back, supporting it.

clue.text: City seller of perfume

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a vender is someone who sells

explanation.surface: An urban perfume merchant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender water is a perfume made from the fragrant plant.

clue.text: Smells of fishing-boats

definitions.meaning: has a taste or whiff of, as in a plan that has a touch of greed
single-masted sailing vessels used for fishing

explanation.surface: Something reeks of trawlers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface joins 'of fishing-boats', but the clue splits after 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to suggest or carry a trace of; the noun sense is a type of small fishing vessel.

clue.text: Private papers destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of the word are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Confidential documents have been shredded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges PAPERS. 'Private' reads as secret but means a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is a private soldier in the Royal Engineers.

clue.text: Tool used by painter making up a last composition

indicators.note: composition means putting the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A painter's tool is used to make up a final painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges UP A LAST; 'making' is a link word, and 'up' is fodder, not part of 'making up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters use a flat blade, also called a palette knife, to mix and spread paint.

clue.text: Play about at a certain level in society

indicators.note: about means the play word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar casually

explanation.surface: Messing about at a particular social level.
explanation.walkthrough: STRUM goes 'about' AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer, and in society a social class or rank.

clue.text: Aspire to keep union leader in funds

indicators.note: keep means the funds word holds the leader letter inside it

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money, funds

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of union

explanation.surface: A trade union boss is maintained with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union leader' looks like a trade union official, but is just U, kept in PURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pursue a goal is to strive or aim for it.

clue.text: Cause of pain in doleful ceremony

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Something painful happens during a sad ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across dolefUL CERemony.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is a painful open sore.

clue.text: Stop that butterfly!

definitions.meaning: a punctuation mark marking a pause
a British butterfly with a white mark on its wing

explanation.surface: A cry to catch a fluttering insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation sense is a pause mark; the insect sense names a butterfly with jagged wings.

clue.text: Game first received at Christmas, going by air

definitions.text: Game first received at Christmas, going by air

parts.words: Game first received at Christmas, going by air
parts.note: a game bird given on the first day of Christmas in the carol, here sent by air mail

explanation.surface: A game bird arrives by air as the first Christmas present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' opens with a bird in a pear tree, the first gift received.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's first-day gift is a game bird shot for sport.

clue.text: Teacher's pet, almost

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the pet word is dropped

parts.note: a rabbit is a common household pet

explanation.surface: The teacher's favourite pupil, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' suggests a favourite pupil; split it as 'Teacher is pet, almost'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher.

clue.text: Dropping off old merchant seamen in water off Cowes

indicators.note: in tells us the old seamen go inside the stretch of water

parts.note: the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight, where Cowes is, and mainland England
MN stands for Merchant Navy

explanation.surface: Retired sailors are lowered into the water off a yachting town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the old seamen inside the water. Cowes is a yachting town on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Somnolent means drowsy, on the verge of nodding off.

clue.text: Litter can make you fret

definitions.meaning: a family of young animals born or hatched together
worry or dwell anxiously on something

explanation.surface: Rubbish lying around can make you anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make you' is a link phrase between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a family of young hatched together; the verb is to dwell on worries.

clue.text: Give new order to please pass by

indicators.note: give new order to means rearrange the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A request to reshuffle things, please, then move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give new order to' rearranges PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or goes by.

clue.text: Half of them given beer that's sour

indicators.note: half of here takes the back two of the four letters of them

parts.note: bitter is a type of English beer

explanation.surface: Some of them drank beer that had gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes EM, the second half of THEM. Bitter is a hoppy British draught beer.
explanation.definitionFit: To embitter someone is to make them resentful, souring their outlook.
